newsitem.title: UK: US, European shares make progress, dollar mixed.
newsitem.headline: US, European shares make progress, dollar mixed.

text.p: Wall Street and European bourses rose in pre-Christmas holiday business on Wednesday, setting aside recent jitters over future prospects for now.

The New York stock market, the world's largest, had rebounded on Tuesday after U.S. interest rates were held steady and rose a further 0.4 percent in the first hour of business, supported by a steady bond market.
On the foreign exchanges, the pound took centre stage, gaining ground after news of a 95,800 drop in British unemployment last month.

The dollar was boosted against the mark after a slowdown in German money supply growth left faint hopes for a cut in the key German money rate. But it was weaker against the yen after news of the first rise in Japan's trade surplus for two years.
Share trading in London, Europe's busiest stock market, was spiced with a little takeover bid speculation but traders said business was likely to be thin ahead of the holiday.

"We've had a good, if predictable morning," the head of sales and trading at a large brokerage said. "But volumes are nothing to speak about. We've seen some selective buying but otherwise it's been pretty quiet."
Investors continue to fret about the risk of a more pronounced drop on Wall Street, which still shows a 26 percent advance this year, even after recent weakness, dealers said.

But British shares shrugged off the sharp drop in jobless numbers, which prompted fear of higher interest rates. A more influential market factor was news of an agreed 1.267 billion pound ($2.1 billion) bid by U.S. group Entergy for London Electricity, which set the market rumour mills running.

News that British November unemployment fell 95,800 to 1.93 million -- much more than a forecast 26,000 decline -- and that retail sales rose 0.7 percent rather than a forecast 0.5 percent did, however, jolt the bond market.
"(It is) very strong data which will certainly increase pressure on the Chancellor(of Exchequer Kenneth Clarke)to increase rates," said Andrew Snowball, economist at the Cooperative Bank.
In Paris shares were aided by the Dow's gains and higher bonds, buoyed by prospects for lower French interest rates. But dealers said volume was modest.

Wall Street's revival helped German shares make a firm start, too, as did a firmer dollar -- good news for exporters -- and weaker-than-expected German money supply data. But gains were more limited later.
The Bundesbank said growth in its main monetary policy indicator, M3 money supply, slowed to an annualised rate of 8.0 percent in November from 8.4 percent in October.
German economists said it did not change their view that the central bank was unlikely to amend its policy just now.
The currency market, however, lived in hope of lower German rates and boosted the dollar against the mark as a result.
"The M3 data was just soft enough to keep interest in Thursday's meeting alive," said one trader at a British bank.
The Bundesbank central council meets for the last time this year on Thursday and is set to announce its 1997 M3 growth targets at a news conference afterwards.

"You can't rule out a (Bundesbank repo rate) cut Thursday but I would still be a bit sceptical, given that M3 growth is still likely to end the year above target," said Peter Von Maydell, senior currency economist at UBS in London.

Market analysts said there was a slight chance the bank might shave its three percent securities repurchase rate. Speculation on such a move grew after the Bank of France trimmed its key money rate to 3.15 percent from 3.20 on Tuesday.
On Wednesday, French call money eased to 3-3/16 5/16 from 3-1/4 3/8, giving hope of more rate reductions, analysts said.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5545 marks and 113.60 yen, compared with 1.5454 and 113.73 in late business on Monday.
The pound rallied to 2.6011 marks from 2.5845 overnight.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was up 32.6 at 4,012.2.
In Frankfurt, the 30-share DAX ended floor trade up 5.62 at 2,820.75 but slipped to around 2,817 in later electronic trade. In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 24.01 at 2,217.71.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $368.70 in the afternoon versus $369 in the morning and a previous close of $368.95. Silver was one cent lower at $4.86.
